newsitem.title: USA: UN okays 3 Iraq oil spot contracts for 1.3m bbls.
newsitem.headline: UN okays 3 Iraq oil spot contracts for 1.3m bbls.

text.p: The United Nations said Wednesday it approved three more oil contracts under the oil-for-food deal with Iraq.
The three "spot" sales were for a total volume of 1.3 million barrels, a U.N. spokesman said.
The three spot deals -- for 450,000 barrels, 750,000 barrels and 100,000 barrels -- bring the total amount sold under the accord to slightly more than 119 million barrels, diplomats said.

The accord allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over a 180-day period starting last Dec 10. The U.N. subsequently agreed to allow that amount to rise by about $70 million in each 90-day period in order to meet Turkish pipeline expenses.
With the latest sale, which at current prices would be valued at about $22 million, the total amount sold under the deal would be about $110 million short of the target, diplomats estimated.

The flow of oil during the first 90-day period was an average of nearly 580,000 barrels a day and that has risen to more than 740,000 bpd in the second 90-day period as oil prices have fallen by around 30 percent.
